# Go 1.27 support

golem's analyzable language version is the version of the toolchain that
**built** golem, not the `go` directive in its `go.mod`. Analysing a module that
declares `go 1.27` with a golem built by Go 1.26 does not degrade gracefully: it
type-checks the package as 1.26, emits `package requires newer Go version`, and
then reports zero sources, zero sinks and zero call edges for the whole module.
golem therefore requires Go 1.27 to build, and CI pins `^1.27.0`.

## What Go 1.27 changes for a Go analyzer

| Change | Effect on golem |
| --- | --- |
| Generic methods — a method may declare its own type parameters | `x/tools` before v0.49.0 type-checks these as `method must have no type parameters` and then reports `undefined: U` for every use of the method's own type parameter. Fixed by the `x/tools` bump; the taint engine still loses the flow (defect 33). |
| Struct literal keys may be any valid field selector, i.e. a promoted field of an embedded struct | `x/tools` v0.39.0 `go/ssa` **panics** — `unexpected expr: *ast.KeyValueExpr` from `(*builder).compLit`. Fixed by the `x/tools` bump; the taint engine still loses the flow (defect 34). |
| Generalized function type inference | No action; inference happens before golem sees types. |
| `encoding/json/v2` and `encoding/json/jsontext` are the default JSON implementation | Modelled in `internal/models/stdlib.json`, mirroring the `encoding/json` entries, and pinned by the `jsonv2-roundtrip` corpus fixture. Without them every JSON round-trip flow in a 1.27 codebase is lost, since the v1 models match on package path. |
| `crypto/mldsa` (FIPS 204 ML-DSA) | Added to `cryptoImportFamilies` and `cryptoSymbolCatalog`, per parameter set, so the CBOM can distinguish a quantum-ready build from a classical one. `crypto/mlkem`, `crypto/sha3`, `crypto/hkdf`, `crypto/pbkdf2`, `crypto/ecdsa`, `crypto/ecdh` and `crypto/rc4` were missing too and are added in the same pass. |
| `uuid`, `simd`, `simd/archsimd` | Not modelled. `simd` is `GOEXPERIMENT`-gated and has no security-relevant surface yet. |
| `go/types.Hasher`, `go/scanner.Scanner.End`, `go/constant.StringLen` | Not used. `Hasher` is a candidate for the access-path type keys in `internal/seam`, which currently key on `Type.String()`. |
| `gotypesalias` GODEBUG removed; `Alias` nodes always produced | golem never set it and does not switch on `*types.Alias`, so aliases are followed through `Underlying()` as before. |
| macOS 12 support dropped | CI runners are `macos-15`; no action. |
| ppc64 big-endian moves to ELFv2 | Release builds target `ppc64le`; no action. |

## Open defects pinned by new corpus fixtures

Both are in the taint engine, not in loading or type-checking: golem records the
correct `usages[]` and the correct `securitySignals` for each fixture, and the
call graph is built, but the data-flow pass reports `sourceCount: 0`.

- **Defect 33** — `testdata/corpus/generic-method`. Taint does not cross a
  generic method, whether the receiver is generic (`Box[T].Map[U]`) or not
  (`Carrier.Unwrap[T]`). Pre-1.27 generics are unaffected: `generic-container`
  and `generic-constraint-method` still report their flow. The likely cause is
  that `fn.Origin()`-keyed summaries in `internal/seam/summary.go` assume the
  function's type parameters all come from the receiver, so a method whose own
  type parameter list is disjoint from the receiver's does not resolve to a
  summary.
- **Defect 34** — `testdata/corpus/promoted-field-literal-key`. Taint entering a
  struct through a promoted key in a composite literal is lost. Reduced to one
  line: `Wrapper{Cmd: r.FormValue("cmd")}` reports no source, while the
  assignment form `w.Cmd = r.FormValue("cmd")` in the same `go 1.27` module
  reports the flow. The access-path code in `internal/seam/accesspath.go` and
  `fieldMemoryKey` in `internal/analyzer/dataflow.go` both address fields by
  index within the immediately enclosing struct, which for a promoted key is not
  the struct named in the literal.

## What the upgrade moved

`x/tools` goes v0.39.0 -> v0.49.0 in the same change, because v0.39.0 is what
panics on the new struct-literal keys. That shifts six of the eight golden
digests, all regenerated in this change and all in the direction of a better
graph:

| Fixture | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `go-chi-exported-roots` | 274 -> 267 nodes, 2470 -> 2372 edges, 65 -> 58 synthetic nodes; the drop is entirely `interface` edges (1038 -> 940). |
| `go-test-bench-security` | 1151 -> 1022 nodes, 6419 -> 6687 edges, 304 -> 180 synthetic nodes; 1778 -> 2056 `func-value` edges. Data flow is byte-identical. |
| `shiftleft-go-demo-all` | 779 -> 903 edges, from `func-value` 222 -> 292 and `interface` 303 -> 357. |
| `gorilla-mux-*` | unchanged. |

RTA and SSA in v0.49.0 resolve function values that previously became synthetic
roots, so synthetic nodes fall and real `func-value` edges rise.

The one loss worth watching: `go-test-bench-all` reports 218 -> 204 slices and
194 -> 182 unique flows, mostly `http-input->external-service` (42 -> 35), with
`dependencyCrossingSlices` 122 -> 108. `go-test-bench-security`, the mode the
tool ships in by default, is unchanged, so the loss is confined to `all` mode
against the labelled benchmark and is not yet explained.

## Open: RTA panics on part of the full bench

`golem golden --tier full` (which runs the whole 32-repo bench, not just the
four golden fixtures) dies with

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
golang.org/x/tools/go/callgraph/rta.(*rta).visitFunc(..., 0x0)
	x/tools@v0.49.0/go/callgraph/rta/rta.go:262
```

on one of the non-golden repositories. `visitFunc` reads `f.Blocks` with no nil
check, so a nil function on RTA's worklist is a segfault. `callableFunctions` in
`internal/analyzer/callgraph.go` now filters nil roots before `rta.Analyze`,
which is right regardless, but the panic survives it — so the nil is produced
inside RTA rather than passed in, and this is an upstream `x/tools` defect. The
four golden fixtures and every corpus fixture are unaffected. Bisecting the
manifest to name the repository, and reporting it upstream, is still to do.

## Not done

- `internal/analyzer/dataflow.go:shouldPropagate` (6 package prefixes) and
  `internal/seam/seam.go:isStdlibPropagate` (11) still disagree, and the legacy
  list has no `encoding` prefix, so json/v2 taint propagates under SEAM only.
- No model covers the `uuid` package, and `math/rand` / `math/rand/v2` have no
  insecure-random source entry in either engine.
